[Bluetooth] Keep BluetoothSocketAndroid alive across Disconnect()

BluetoothSocketAndroid::Disconnect() posts DoDisconnect() to the socket
thread with a PostDisconnect() reply on the UI thread, and binds
base::Unretained(this) to both. A caller that drops its last reference
right after Disconnect(), as ~BluetoothSerialPortImpl() does, destroys
the socket before DoDisconnect() runs. The destructor then fails its
CHECK that the Java socket is closed, and the queued tasks would run on
a destroyed object.

Bind the scoped_refptr instead, as Connect(), Receive(), Send() and
BluetoothSocketNet::Disconnect() already do, so the socket stays alive
until PostDisconnect() completes. PostDisconnect() also skips
receiving_thread_ when it was never started or was already stopped by
an earlier Disconnect().

CONV=6a7bb1be-0fb3-44d2-a8b6-eda9d4c235ff

webnn: validate opSupportLimits rank ranges for operators with companion operands

Follow-up to the rank-validation helpers added in the previous CL, for
operators whose buildFn has to synthesise companion operands whose
shapes are derived from the input rank under test:

 - conv2d / convTranspose2d build a filter whose input-channel dim
   matches the input's C dim so the default groups=1 divides evenly.
 - gemm, batchNormalization build the matching second operand / mean /
   variance for the rank being exercised.
 - gru, gruCell, lstm, lstmCell build weight and recurrentWeight from
   the steps / inputSize / hiddenSize implied by the input shape, and
   return the first output of the returned sequence.
 - argMinMax additionally covers every (rank, axis) pair, since the
   valid axis domain depends on the rank under test.

[Extensions] Fix flaky PermissionsApiTest.FileLoad

The test extension's service worker fetches file: URLs as soon as its
script runs. Blink only allows an extension origin to load file: URLs
after the renderer adds the extension's origin access permissions, which
happens in Dispatcher::ActivateExtension() on the renderer main thread.
The browser sends that activation message when the worker context is
initialized, but the worker script keeps running on its own thread, so
the fetches can run before the permissions exist. They then fail with
"Not allowed to load local resource". This happened about 25% of the
time on slow Android desktop emulators.

Have the extension send a "ready" message and wait for a reply before
running its tests. Before replying, the test flushes the pending
renderer messages with RendererStartupHelper::FlushAllForTesting(), so
the activation has been handled.

Verified by adding a 1 second sleep in Dispatcher::ActivateExtension():
the test then failed every time without this change and passed with it.

[a11y] Skip DOM child traversal when clearing empty accessibility nodes

This change reduces Blink accessibility CPU time by 0.88% and overall
renderer main thread (`CrRendererMain`) CPU time by 0.20% in Speedometer
3. Specifically, it reduces CPU time in `AXObject::ClearChildren` by
27.09%.

Previously, Blink walked all DOM child nodes when clearing accessibility
children, even for objects without attached children. During initial
tree construction, new accessibility objects have no attached children
yet. Now, each accessibility object tracks whether any child links to it
as a parent. Blink skips the DOM child traversal when no children link
to the parent object. This change does not alter accessibility behavior.

Revert CHECK back to DCHECK for relative path result in SerializeURLImpl

When serializing FileSystemAccess URLs, relative path calculations can
fail in certain valid situations where the URL path cannot be made
relative to the root permission path. Revert the CHECK back to a DCHECK
to prevent crashes in release builds while the conditions under which
this occurs are investigated.

This fix was generated by the Crash Autofix pipeline for crash report
crash/ee2f1c9908400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more details.

[metrics] Open histogram XML files one at a time

The histogram allowlist presubmit opens all XML files before parsing any
of them. With 346 files (currently in tree), it fails under a MacOS
descriptor limit of 256 with error: OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open
files.

Pass filenames to ElementTree so it closes each file after parsing,
including on errors. Update the CLI and WebView caller to use the same
approach, while retaining support for caller-owned streams used by
historical histogram comparisons.

Honor spellcheck attribute on nested elements in cold mode spell check

In ColdModeSpellCheckRequester::QualifyingEditable, the condition for
qualifying the editable root checked:
`!element->IsSpellCheckingEnabled() || !SpellChecker::IsSpellCheckingEnabledAt(position)`

Checking `element->IsSpellCheckingEnabled()` (where element is the
HighestEditableRoot) prevented cold mode spell checking from qualifying
an editable when the focused child had `spellcheck="true"` inside a
root marked `spellcheck="false"`.

Because `SpellChecker::IsSpellCheckingEnabledAt(position)` already
traverses the ancestor chain from `position` up to the root editable
to determine enablement at the closest ancestor, checking only
`!SpellChecker::IsSpellCheckingEnabledAt(position)` correctly honors
nested spellcheck attributes in both directions (mirroring
HotModeSpellCheckRequester).

Add unit tests covering both nested spellcheck="true" and
spellcheck="false" in cold mode.

[crubit] Add `cc_std` bindings for `std::optional`.

This CL adds `//build/rust/crubit:cc_std` - Rust bindings for the C++
standard library (initially only covering `<optional>`).  `cc_std`
becomes an implicitly injected dependency of all `rust_api_from_cpp`
bindings.

This CL also enables the `layout_compat_optional` Crubit feature.  This
means that `std::optional<T>` is represented in Rust as
layout-compatible `cc_std::std::optional<T>` (or
`cc_std::std::trivial_optional<T>`) rather than being bridged to
`Option<T>`.  Conversions from/to `Option<T>` are explicit (e.g.
`.into()`).

[event-timing] Fix target frame attribution and verify source window in CanExposeNode

PointerEventManager lives on the local-root frame and dispatches pointer
and compatibility mouse events to targets that may belong to same-process
child frames. Previously, PointerEventManager::DispatchPointerEvent and
MouseEventManager::DispatchMouseEvent constructed UIEventTiming scoped to
`frame_` (the local-root frame) rather than the target node's frame. When
an event targeted a subframe node, EventDispatcher::Dispatch subsequently
set `event.target()` to that subframe node, causing the outer
UIEventTiming scope on the local-root frame to record an entry on the
parent frame's WindowPerformance whose `target_` referenced the child
frame's DOM Node.

This CL provides a surgical fix in two layers (with a follow-up CL
removing the outer UIEventTiming wrappers entirely):

1. Attribute UIEventTiming to `target_node->GetDocument().GetFrame()` in
   `PointerEventManager::DispatchPointerEvent` and
   `MouseEventManager::DispatchMouseEvent` (via a 3-argument
   `UIEventTiming(handling_frame, target_frame, event)` constructor,
   guarded by a default-enabled Finch kill-switch feature flag
   `kEventTimingUseTargetFrame`) so that events dispatched to subframe
   targets are recorded only against the target's frame.
2. Update `Performance::CanExposeNode(Node*, const DOMWindow* source)`
   and all of its callers (`PerformanceEventTiming`,
   `PerformanceElementTiming`, `PerformanceContainerTiming`,
   `PerformanceScrollTiming`, `LargestContentfulPaint`,
   `LayoutShiftAttribution`, and `WindowPerformance::AddScrollTiming`) to
   require `node->GetDocument().domWindow() == source`.

In addition to providing defense-in-depth against cross-frame node
exposure, checking `document.domWindow() == source` in
`Performance::CanExposeNode` brings Blink into closer compliance with the
Web Performance "get an element" algorithm
(https://wicg.github.io/element-timing/#sec-get-an-element, referenced by
`PerformanceEventTiming.target`, `LargestContentfulPaint.element`,
`PerformanceElementTiming.element`, etc.). The spec passes `this`'s
relevant global object's associated `Document` (`source->document()`) and
requires that the element's shadow-including root is that exact
`Document`, returning `null` if the node belongs to or was adopted into
another document.

Finally, to help evaluate field impact on main-frame-only RUM observers
that previously received cross-frame subframe interactions, this CL
records `is_main_frame` and `is_cross_frame_target` on
`EventTimingReportingInfo` and logs three new variants of
`Blink.Responsiveness.UserInteraction.MaxEventDuration`:
- `.MainFrame` (interactions targeting the main frame directly)
- `.CrossFrameTarget` (interactions where `handling_frame != target_frame`)
- `.MainFrameIncludingCrossFrameTarget` (combined baseline matching what
  was previously reported to the main frame)

Resolve VirtualDocumentPath with File::Error status

VirtualDocumentPath reduced every lookup outcome to a nullable URI. A
missing document, a permission denial, an incomplete EXTRA_LOADING
listing and a provider exception all returned null, so mkdir() and
createOrOpen() could attempt to create a document or directory when a
listing had not finished yet. Lookup also took the first cursor row when
two documents shared a display name, and did not verify that
intermediate path segments or the tree root were directories.

Export base::File::Error to Java as org.chromium.base.FileError through
java_cpp_enum and add VirtualDocumentPath::ResolveDocument()
(resolveDocument() in Java). Lookup scans the whole cursor, reports
duplicate rows matching the same display name as
FILE_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION, reports an EXTRA_LOADING or null cursor as
FILE_ERROR_FAILED rather than FILE_ERROR_NOT_FOUND, and requires
intermediate segments and the tree root to be directories. Also reject
dot and NUL relative-path segments during parsing. Existing
ResolveToContentUri(), mkdir(), and createOrOpen() callers delegate to
resolveDocument() and only attempt creation on FILE_ERROR_NOT_FOUND.

[Glic] Remove legacy drag-and-drop drag source plumbing

Second of two CLs; see crrev.com/c/8419795 for the replacement path.

Deletes content::DragSourceMap, content::DragSourceDocumentTracker,
WebContents::FromDragId, and
RenderWidgetHostDelegate::OnDragSourceEnded, as drag source eligibility
and provenance are now captured at drag start via
WebContentsObserver::DidStartDrag.

Completes the cleanup for b:553152493: that report described Glic
attaching the embedding tab's full annotated page context when a drag
originated in a cross-origin iframe, because WebContents::FromDragId
widened subframe provenance to the containing tab. Rather than adding an
origin comparison, crrev.com/c/8419795 stops attaching TabContext to
drag-and-drop AdditionalContext entirely, and this CL removes
WebContents::FromDragId and its backing tracker.

Task Manager: Adopt safe JNI pointers for TaskManagerObserverAndroid

TaskManagerServiceBridge.addObserver() previously handed the native
TaskManagerObserverAndroid to Java as a raw long, and removeObserver()
passed that address back across JNI for manual deletion. Express Java's
ownership in the type system by returning a JniUniquePtr from
addObserver() and destroying it directly via JniUniquePtr.destroy().
ObserverHandle is kept so that TaskManagerMediator does not depend on
the JNI pointer type.

No behavior change for correct callers. Removing an observer twice is
now a no-op instead of a double delete.

TAG=agy
CONV=0bfa03dc-e65b-4b30-b71a-bad41af6b0c8

Fix filterable-select-keyboard-behavior.tentative.html failures

This patch fixes two failure modes in
filterable-select-keyboard-behavior.tentative.html:

1. StartFiltering() and StopFiltering() were previously called in
   TextFieldInputType::HandleFocusInEvent and HandleBlurEvent. However,
   Document::SetFocusedElement skips dispatching focus/focusin/blur
   events when GetPage()->GetFocusController().IsFocused() is false. On
   macOS headless_shell, RenderWidgetHostViewMac::Focus() posts
   SetPageFocus(true) asynchronously, so focusing the filter <input>
   early during test load did not call StartFiltering() to set
   :active-option. Moving StartFiltering() and StopFiltering() to
   HTMLInputElement::SetFocused (when focus_type != FocusType::kPage)
   ensures :active-option is updated synchronously when the input gains
   or loses focus regardless of page focus state.

2. Adding the 5th subtest in https://crrev.com/c/8490185 increased the
   number of sequential WebDriver actions enough to exceed the default
   10s WPT timeout on several bots. Adding <meta name=timeout
   content=long> prevents the test from timing out.

[LHS] Embed expanded LHS iframe directly in chrome://new-tab-page

Removes the intermediate `chrome-untrusted://new-tab-page/expanded-lhs`
iframe and embeds the expanded LHS URL
(`https://www.google.com/search?nem=341`) directly inside
`<cr-left-hand-side>` via `<ntp-iframe id="expanded">`.

1. Moves `expandedLhsUrl` resolution (including the `atvm=3` hybrid mode
parameter and forced embedded page host overrides) from
`UntrustedSource` into `NewTabPageUI` `loadTimeData`.

2. Explicitly allowlists `google_base_url` in `NewTabPageUI`'s
`child-src` Content Security Policy.

3. Forwards the `allow` attribute on `<ntp-iframe>` to its inner
`<iframe>` so `allow="unbounded-element"` is preserved.

4. Removes `expanded-lhs` handling, unit tests, and `expanded_lhs.html`
from `UntrustedSource`.

[css-mixins] Rewrite @private names with stylesheet registry (2.1/N)

Replace StyleRulePrivate and CSSPrivateVariable with selectorless
StyleRules storing declarations as internal -ua-private- custom
properties.

Each StyleSheetContents owns a private PropertyRegistry that maps
internal names to authored names and stores optional type registrations.
It is shared by stylesheet wrappers, copied during copy-on-write, and
excluded from the registered custom property namespace.

Declarations with the same authored name and nearest style-rule ancestor
reuse an internal name, while nested style rules receive distinct names.
CSSPrivateRule reverse-maps them for serialization.

[GlassFrame] Avoid calling ThemeChanged() on window activation

Previously, BrowserWidget subscribed to GlassFrameService eligibility
changes to call Widget::ThemeChanged() and mutated
ui::ColorProviderKey::frame_style to FrameStyle::kGlass when eligible.
Because GlassFrameService limits the glass effect to a single active
window, switching between browser windows caused glass eligibility to
flip on both the deactivated and newly activated windows. Mutating
ColorProviderKey and calling Widget::ThemeChanged() on both windows
forced a full theme invalidation across the Views hierarchy and all
WebContents (which includes the WebUI toolbar).

This CL moves the remaining glass-specific tab strip color calculations
out of AddMaterialTabStripColorMixer and remove FrameStyle::kGlass:
- Apply the 80% opacity for selected tabs in a glass frame directly in
  TabStyle::GetTabBackgroundColor(..., bool frame_glass, ...).
- Add set_paint_transparent_for_glass() and a glass eligibility
  subscription to TabStripControlButton so that tab strip scroll
  buttons and NewTabButton update their transparent background
  when glass eligibility changes without requiring
  Widget::ThemeChanged().
- Remove FrameStyle::kGlass from ColorProviderKey and remove the
  ThemeChanged() callback from BrowserWidget.

[Fortify] Set initiating_frame_id for clipboard content analysis

Clipboard paste and copy scans did not set initiating_frame_id, so
frame_url_chain fell back to the focused frame. A page could move focus
to another iframe before the scan started and have the wrong frame
checked against iframe-scoped DLP rules.

Set initiating_frame_id from the ClipboardEndpoint's RenderFrameHost, so
the chain starts from the frame that triggered the action.

Always get PdfInfo and update params in TabImpl#loadUrl

TabImpl#getPdfInfoAndUpdateLoadUrl() (formerly getPdfInfoForLoadUrl)
updates LoadUrlParams via params.setIsPdf(true) for inline PDF
navigations. Previously, it was only evaluated inside the
!mIsNativePageCommitPending guard. When a new loadUrl() arrived while a
previous native page navigation was still pending commit,
params.setIsPdf(true) was skipped for content:// and file:// PDF
navigations.

Rename getPdfInfoForLoadUrl() to getPdfInfoAndUpdateLoadUrl() and call
it unconditionally before checking mIsNativePageCommitPending so
params.setIsPdf(true) is always set.

LHS: Lay out the LHS beside the RHS

...instead of on top of it. Now that the RHS elements' break points
reference the RHS width, the LHS is a flex item next to #rhsWrapper
rather than position: fixed, and the RHS shrinks to make room for it.

Other changes:
- Since the page can't scroll without moving the LHS with it, the RHS now scrolls on its own.
- The OneGoogleBar scrim's scrolled-to-top state now follows #rhsContent instead of the document.
- The clip-path is sized 0x0, so that it doesn't take up invisible space on top of LHS.

Screencast: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTU0Mzc2ODg0ODU5Njk5MnwyMmVjMzkxMi1lOQ

Prevent scripts from forcefully initiating drags on mousedown

This CL patches the scenario where a script-initiated window move causes
a drag to start even if the user did not move their pointer after doing
a mouse down.

This CL addresses this issue by calculating the drag threshold distance
in physical screen coordinates rather than logical relative coordinates.
The window moving after a mouse down will have no effect since the
pointer didn't move past the in-screen threshold.

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dnd.html#security-risks-in-the-drag-and-drop-model

ash: Require parent access approval for child timezone changes

Previously, the Parent Access Code (PAC) dialog for timezone changes
in ChromeOS Settings was only enforced in the WebUI frontend. A child
user could bypass this check by invoking chrome.settingsPrivate.setPref
directly from the DevTools console.

This CL records per-user timezone change approval state (keyed by
AccountId) in ParentAccessService when parent access validation
succeeds in NewDateTimeHandler, and invalidates it when
NewDateTimeHandler is destroyed (i.e. when the Settings page closes).
settingsPrivate checks whether the user associated with the Profile is
allowed to modify timezone prefs (generated timezone resolution prefs,
cros.system.timezone, and settings.timezone) via the shared
IsTimezoneChangeAllowed() helper.

[ttc][android] Treat a paused window as visible

TtcSessionMediator only treated STARTED and RESUMED activities as
visible, but a paused activity is still on screen: an unfocused window
in multi-window mode, or a window behind the microphone permission
dialog. Rename isActivityStarted() to isActivityVisible() and include
PAUSED_WITH_NATIVE, which affects both callers:

- A window that is paused when its profile becomes available now joins
  the TtcSessionWindowTracker, so it keeps the session alive.
- A microphone grant delivered while the activity is still paused
  behind the permission dialog now starts the session instead of being
  dropped.

Revert "[Omnibox] Defer AI Mode popup creation"

This reverts commit 7a7e498dbdb75a1c7329d8e7bf4395e3c5832fb2.

Reason for revert:
OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreationPendingBrowserTest.ClassicPopupContextMenuCreatesAimContent
added by the original CL is consistently failing on
mac26-arm64-rel-tests

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/mac26-arm64-rel-tests/4653/overview

Original change's description:
> [Omnibox] Defer AI Mode popup creation
>
> Design doc:
> https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P7h7q6zqhxgPtKhVJBUAU9eb1pawDwK66iQu8CTeRSs/edit?resourcekey=0-nPCcl7S22YgfphQ-H6WV5Q&tab=t.0
>
> When a browser window is built, OmniboxPopupAimPresenter creates the AI
> Mode popup's WebUI content in its constructor: a WebContents and its
> navigation to the AI Mode popup page. The navigation's IPCs and the
> page load then compete with the new window's first frame on the browser
> UI thread and in the shared top-chrome renderer. The AI Mode popup is
> opened far less often than the regular results popup, so it does not
> need to be ready that early.
>
> This CL adds a disabled-by-default feature,
> OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation. With it, the presenter does not create
> the content in its constructor. It overrides the new
> OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::CreateWebUIContent(), and
> OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::EnsureWebUIContentCreated() calls it on
> whichever of these comes first:
>
> - A task posted after the browser window presents its first frame.
> - OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::Show().
> - The regular popup's context menu, which acts on the AI Mode
>   WebContents.
>
> The presenter asks for that frame itself: its constructor makes a
> one-off RequestSuccessfulPresentationTimeForNextFrame() call on the
> compositor of the location bar's widget. Both LocationBarView and
> WebUILocationBar build the presenter while the window is built, before
> its first paint, so the next frame is the window's first frame. The
> presenter posts the creation task at most once.
>
> The presentation task is what keeps the work out of the window's first
> frame. A fixed delay from window creation could not do that: on Linux
> and macOS the window is activated inside its own show call, before the
> first paint, and the time to first paint varies by device. There is
> also no fallback timer. A requested callback is kept until a frame
> presents successfully. A window that is never presented never shows
> the popup either, and the on-show path covers any open. A presenter
> that is created after the first paint, because the profile became
> eligible for AI Mode later, gets the next presented frame or its first
> show.
>
> With the feature disabled, creation is unchanged.
>
>   out/Default/browser_tests \
>   --gtest_filter='OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation*:*WithoutDeferCreation' && \
>   out/Default/unit_tests \
>   --gtest_filter='OmniboxPopupPresenterBaseTest.*'
>

hid: Filter reports with top-level collection

FilterCollectionReports evaluates HasReportInAlwaysProtectedCollection
and HasReportInCollectionWithUsagePage using the original_collection
argument. When recursing into child collections, original_collection
referred to the child collection node rather than the top-level
collection (TLC).

In standard HID topologies (e.g. boot mice conforming to HID 1.11
Appendix E.10), report items reside inside nested Physical collections
under an Application TLC. Because HasReportInAlwaysProtectedCollection
gates on collection_type == kHIDCollectionTypeApplication, it evaluated
to false for child collections, leaking always-protected report
descriptor metadata via HIDDevice.collections[].children[].inputReports
on non-Windows platforms.

This change threads original_top_level_collection through recursive
invocations so that always-protected and FIDO reports are evaluated
against the containing top-level collection. This aligns Chromium with
the WebHID specification and restores parity with runtime I/O filtering
in HidConnection::IsReportProtected.

Initial upload: base registry utilities and shared security descriptors

[remoting] Add Windows registry utilities and shared security descriptors

Introduces shared registry helper functions in //remoting/base for
Windows:
- WriteDefaultStringValue(): writes the default string value for a key,
  creating it if necessary.
- WriteDefaultStringValueBothViews(): writes the default string value
  across default, 32-bit, and 64-bit views.
- DeleteKeyBothViews(): deletes a key across default, 32-bit, and 64-bit
  views.
- DeleteKeyIfEmpty(): deletes a key only if it contains no subkeys and
  no values.

Also extracts shared security descriptor strings for pairing registry
secrets and RDP desktop session COM permissions into
remoting/host/win/security_descriptor.h to allow sharing between the
host daemon and native installer.

Improve edge cases with <selectedcontent> updating

This patch implements feedback in the HTML PR for <selectedcontent>
element updates: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12263

- Decouples <selectedcontent> updates from ResetToDefaultSelection() and
  adds ResetSelectedness() to only update <selectedcontent> when an
  option's selectedness actually changes (including when select.size,
  select.multiple, option.disabled, or optgroup.disabled changes, or
  when an option is removed).
- Updates <selectedcontent> on form.reset(), when option.selected is
  set to false, and when re-assigning option.selected = true on an
  already-selected option.
- Avoids redundant <selectedcontent> updates during atomic moves within
  the same <select> or when setting option.selected = false on an
  already-unselected option in a single-select listbox.

This patch is mostly tested by this upstream WPT PR:
https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/62242

Replace StringPrintf with StrCat to remove heavy include

Refactoring the building of this error string lets us remove the heavy
include, and also simplifies the code to avoid multiple conversions
to/from ASCII and UTF16.

Adds missing includes as needed to fix the build.

Should save ~74 MiB of compiler input size with `use_clang_modules`
enabled and ~10x that with it off.

[Reading mode PDFs] Treat list items as distilled content

Add kListItem to the rules-based content roles. This is a no-op for
PDFs until list detection lands. For other pages distilled with Screen2x
(e.g. after a Readability fallback), non-collapsed list items are now
picked as whole content nodes, instead of only the paragraphs inside
them plus whatever Screen2x picks. Collapsed list items are still
searched rather than picked, so aria-expanded handling is unchanged.

[extensions] Comment fixes from the enterprise.webrtc review

The dictionary keys in webrtc_internals.cc stopped being internal to
chrome://webrtc-internals once enterprise.webrtc began forwarding them.
The peer connection record reaches onPeerConnectionAdded verbatim and
the getUserMedia keys reach getSnapshot through the rename table in
webrtc_diagnostics_impl.cc, so a rename there is an extension API
change.

The webidl comments are the public API reference, so getUserMedia,
getCaptureStatus, origins and the incognito manifest value now carry
the <code> and $(ref:) markup the rest of the directory uses.

Use pidfd_open + ppoll in WaitpidWithTimeout on Linux/ChromeOS/Android

In WaitpidWithTimeout() (base/process/process_posix.cc), waiting for a
child process with a finite timeout previously polled waitpid(WNOHANG)
in an exponential-backoff usleep() loop that reaches 262,144 us
(~262 ms) after ~60 ms. Because SIGCHLD is set to SIG_DFL by default
without an installed signal handler, usleep() is not interrupted when a
child exits. Any child running longer than ~60 ms (such as browser test
subprocesses in TestLauncher and utility subprocesses cleaned up via
BrowserProcessIOThread::ProcessHostCleanUp()) therefore sat as an
unreaped zombie for up to 262 ms (~131 ms on average) after _exit().

Add a WaitWithPidfd() helper on Linux, ChromeOS, and Android that opens
a pidfd via pidfd_open(2) and blocks in ppoll(2) until the child exits
or the timeout expires, waking immediately when the child terminates and
falling back to the existing usleep() loop only if pidfd_open is
unavailable. Also return early after the initial waitpid(WNOHANG) check
if the process has already exited or the requested wait duration is
zero.

On linux-chromeos-rel browser_tests, eliminating the post-exit polling
delay cuts per-test subprocess reaping overhead by ~130-250 ms per test
(saving ~1.0-1.5 s of wall-clock time across a 21-test parallel batch at
--test-launcher-jobs=8, and ~100+ minutes of cumulative subprocess wait
time across the ~48,900 tests in browser_tests).

[Omnibox] Show optional button after navigating away from the NTP

Navigating from the NTP to a page (e.g. via a Most Visited tile) commits
the new URL while the NTP native page is still attached; it is only
removed by TabImpl.hideNativePage() on first paint.
LocationBarCoordinator.shouldShowOptionalButton() checked
NewTabPageDelegate#isCurrentlyVisible(), which is still true at that
point, so the button was hidden. Nothing re-evaluates the button when
the native page is later removed, because ToolbarPhone's visual state
has already switched to NORMAL. Check the URL instead, matching
LocationBarPhone#shouldCenterUrlAndStatus().

Reject symlinked parents in PrepareNativeLocalFileForWritableApp

PrepareNativeLocalFileForWritableApp() rejects links via base::IsLink()
and FLAG_NO_FOLLOW, but both apply only to the final path component. If
an intermediate directory component is a symlink, path resolution
follows it, so neither check detects it. FLAG_OPEN_ALWAYS then creates
the file inside the link's target directory rather than at the requested
location, and for directories DirectoryExists() succeeds on the target.

ValidateFileEntryAndGetPath() can now also return the root path of the
granted file or directory. getWritableEntry() passes this root to
PrepareFilesForWritableApp(), which checks each path component from the
target up to the root and rejects the request if any of them is a
symbolic link. The root and its ancestors are not checked.

[Reading mode PDFs] Filter sub-5px unlabeled images in AXTree builder

Some PDF generators split illustrations into hundreds of 1-pixel-tall
horizontal scanlines or include tiny decorative spacer images. Exposing
each sub-5px slice as a separate unlabeled kImage node floods the
accessibility tree and causes Reading Mode to render each slice as an
individual canvas element with vertical gaps.

When kPdfAccessibilityHeuristicEnhancements is enabled, filter out
unlabeled images with width or height less than 5px in
PdfAccessibilityTreeBuilderHeuristic while preserving small images
that have explicit alt text.

This change is part of the broader effort to support rendering PDF
raster images in Reading Mode (see go/rm-pdf-raster-images for context).

[crubit] Support `extra_rust_sources_mod` in `rust_api_from_cpp`.

Before this CL, `extra_rust_sources` of `rust_api_from_cpp` were always
placed at the root of the generated bindings crate.  This doesn't work
when the hand-written code has to provide items at a specific module
path.  For example, Crubit-generated code expects hand-written types
like `cc_std::std::optional<T>` in the `std` module of `cc_std` (Rust
bindings for the C++ standard library).

After this CL, a new `extra_rust_sources_mod` attribute (e.g.
`"foo::bar"`) places `extra_rust_sources` into a nested module of the
generated bindings.  `rustc` resolves `#[path = ...]` attributes inside
a nested module relative to a matching subdirectory (e.g. `foo/bar/`),
and therefore such `extra_rust_sources` are copied into that
subdirectory of `target_gen_dir`.

The new `ExtraRustSourcesMod` test covers the new attribute.

[TTC] Connect TtcEvalHarness to SessionController and drive canned audio

Connects the evaluation harness to the TTC session controller and engine:
- Connects TtcEvalHarness to SessionControllerImpl via
  SessionController::Observer to drive canned audio injection and
  observe turn lifecycle, transcriptions, tool execution, and errors.
- Adds OnJournalEvent to ConversationObserver to forward server diagnostic
  events (e.g. PageContextVerbalized) from ConversationImpl to observers.
- Handles trailing silence pumping and turn result assembly.
- Populates verbalized_content and journal_events in TurnResult in debug mode.
- Guards against voice plate instantiation in headless/test environments.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests for SessionControllerImpl and TtcEvalHarness.

[icu] Cache thread-local percent NumberFormat in FormatPercent

base::FormatPercent(int) accounts for ~0.44% of browser UI-thread jank
on Windows Stable by constructing and destroying a brand-new
icu::MessageFormat and icu::NumberFormat on every invocation:
http://pprof/?id=794d4ba5ba6d1601b704037660e3dc25&filter=show:FormatPercent&pivot=base::FormatPercent

This CL caches a thread-local icu::NumberFormat percent instance
alongside the icu::Locale it was created for, matching FormatNumber()
and FormatDouble() while automatically recreating the formatter if the
default ICU locale changes at runtime. The new behavior is guarded
behind the existing kI18nOptimizations feature
(features::IsI18nOptimizationsEnabled(), enabled by default).

NumberFormattingPerfTest results on a Lenovo IdeaPad 5 (AMD Ryzen 7
5700U, 8 cores / 16 threads, Windows 11 26200, is_official_build =
true, dcheck_always_on = false, median of 5 runs):
- FormatPercent:
  - Baseline (main): 38,561 ns
  - CL 1/3 (https://crrev.com/c/8564041): 34,156 ns (-11.4%)
  - CL 2/3 (https://crrev.com/c/8573417): 26,315 ns (-23.0% vs. 1/3)
  - CL 3/3 (https://crrev.com/c/8568883): 26,592 ns (+1.1% vs. 2/3)
  - This CL: 441 ns (-98.3% vs. 3/3, -98.9% vs. main)
- FormatPercent_Concurrent (8 threads):
  - Baseline (main): 90,985 ns
  - CL 1/3 (https://crrev.com/c/8564041): 70,910 ns (-22.1%)
  - CL 2/3 (https://crrev.com/c/8573417): 29,452 ns (-58.5% vs. 1/3)
  - CL 3/3 (https://crrev.com/c/8568883): 22,995 ns (-21.9% vs. 2/3)
  - This CL: 817 ns (-96.4% vs. 3/3, -99.1% vs. main)

[Linux] Fix GlobalShortcuts portal binding issues

Fix several issues with how GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux binds
shortcuts with the org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts portal:
- Non-global commands were bound, which showed them in the portal
  dialog, and some backends showed the dialog again whenever they
  changed. Only bind global commands.
- Shortcuts returned by ListShortcuts were sent again along with the
  bound commands, so BindShortcuts could contain duplicate IDs, which
  some backends treat as new shortcuts. Deduplicate the IDs.
- Commands with an empty description were bound without one, and some
  backends ignore such shortcuts. Fall back to the command name.
- A failed BindShortcuts call left the bind state stuck, so commands
  added later were never bound. A failed ListShortcuts call stopped
  binding entirely, even though some backends never list shortcuts.
- Binding was skipped whenever every command was listed, but most
  backends require binding in every session to activate shortcuts.
  Only skip it on version 1 of the interface, which shows a dialog on
  every bind.
- Every bind replaces the shortcuts stored for the app, so listed
  shortcuts of accelerator groups that aren't loaded (e.g. of other
  profiles) were dropped. Pass them through.

Restructure the bind state machine around the set of IDs to bind so
that a bind is only made when the set changes.

Increase Maximum Attempts to Authenticate DRM Device (10 -> 50)

Previously the logic had attempted indefinitely but the previous CL
limited it to 10 times (which waits ~1 sec).

But there is possibility it's too small, according to the comment
(crbug.com/563090726#comment19). Previously it was 30 (~ 3 sec) and
was safe. Also crbug.com/570378657#comment5 confirmed "30" fixes the
failure.

This CL increases the limit from 10 to 50 (which waits ~5 sec) in
including 2 sec margin for safe.

As the side effect, the user may need to wait for 5 sec to recover
on GPU process crash. But I think it's acceptable considering the
failure.

Make CrSelectableMixin#selected property always be a string.

Since Lit reactive properties can't be a union of multiple types, it is
incorrect to have the 'selected' property be of type 'string|number'.

This also causes a "Property type mismatch" error to be thrown from
@webui-eslint/lit-property-accessor in a follow-up CL where ESLint
checks are extended to also apply to Mixins, fixed by changing it to
always be a 'string' type.

FSA: pair move events from across different inotify fd reads

Allow pairing IN_MOVED_TO and IN_MOVED_FROM across event buffers.

Also add a slight delay when polling with an unpaired IN_MOVED_FROM at
the ready:

"""
Applications should also allow for the possibility that the
IN_MOVED_FROM event was the last event that could fit in the buffer
returned by the current call to read(2), and the accompanying
IN_MOVED_TO event might be fetched only on the next read(2), which
should be done with a (small) timeout to allow for the fact that
insertion of the IN_MOVED_FROM+IN_MOVED_TO event pair is not atomic, and
also the possibility that there may not be any IN_MOVED_TO event.
"""

[Omnibox] Register IPH_OmniboxAskGLensIcon promo

Adds the in-product help (IPH) toast that will highlight the Lens icon
in the omnibox popup for the Ask Google about this page experiment.
This CL only registers the promo; nothing triggers it yet. A follow-up
CL shows it from the omnibox popup behind a new `Omnibox_AskGLensIconIph`

  stays within the omnibox popup.

  is pending UX review.

  `kOmniboxNotOpenPrecondition`: its anchor lives in the omnibox popup,
  so it can only show while the omnibox is open. This is the first
  entry in that allowlist.
- Lists `kWebUIOmniboxAskGAboutThisPage` as a required feature in the
  promo metadata.

[glic] Show security interstitials in Gemini in Chrome panel

Committed security interstitials (such as EnterpriseWarnPage) commit as
error documents (NavigationHandle::IsErrorPage() is true). Previously,
GlicWebClientManager classified all error pages as kLoadError, hiding
the guest WebContents behind the error overlay before the user could
interact with the warning.

Add mojom::GuestPageType::kSecurityInterstitial (detected via
SecurityInterstitialTabHelper) so both NoWebview and <webview> hosts
display the interstitial directly:
- Clicking "Proceed" reloads in-place in the same guest WebContents,
  preserving the WebContents-scoped SafeBrowsingAllowlistSet. (Reusing
  kGuestError would trigger reloadAfterNavigation in <webview>,
  recreating the <webview> and wiping out the allowlist; reusing
  kLoadError cannot be spot-checked from the WebUI renderer or left in
  GuestState::kLoading without hiding the interstitial and timing out.)
- Clicking "Go back" (DontProceed) navigates to the default safe page,
  which is blocked by the guest navigation throttle and forwarded via
  OnGuestNavigationBlocked to transition the panel to the error state.

Demo: http://shortn/_L6uNCVtxuj

[net] Lazily start AIA server and cache root CA in EmbeddedTestServer

EmbeddedTestServer::GenerateCertAndKeys() previously created and
started a second HTTP EmbeddedTestServer (aia_http_server_) on every
HTTPS server initialization even when neither OCSP nor
IntermediateType::kByAIA was configured, and re-read and parsed
root_ca_cert.pem from disk on every GenerateCertAndKey() call.

Only create and listen on aia_http_server_ when a certificate config
requires OCSP or AIA intermediate serving, and cache the parsed static
kTestRootCa certificate and private key across calls.

WebMCP: Re-check for a duplicate tool name after serializing inputSchema

`registerTool()` rejects a duplicate tool name up front, but then
serializes `inputSchema`, which can run script (via `toJSON()`) that
registers another tool with the same name. `registerTool()` then still
sends the duplicate to the browser, which kills the renderer.

Check for a duplicate name again after serialization, next to the
existing document-activity re-check, and reject with the same
`InvalidStateError` as the up-front check.

See https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/pull/347 for the spec
fix.

R=khushalsagar

Reset accessibility state on Print Preview reset

`HandleResetPrintPreviewModeMessage()` creates a new engine but left
`accessibility_state_` as `kLoaded`, so `ProposeDocumentLayout()`
reloaded accessibility before the new document finished loading, hitting
`DCHECK(document_loaded_)` in `GetDocumentMetadata()`. Set it back to
kPending so DocumentLoadComplete() reloads it instead.

Also re-enable SystemAccessProcessPrintBrowserTest.
UpdatePrintSettingsPrintableArea on the forced-accessibility bot.

parent
b8aca858b069502dcbe08cf590ffd28f7e9046ec [ diff ] 
WebMCP: Re-check document activity after serializing `inputSchema`

`ModelContext::registerTool()` checks that its document is active up
front, but then serializes `inputSchema`, which can run script via a
`toJSON()` method. If that script makes the document inactive, e.g., by
removing its iframe, `registerTool()` carries on and dereferences the
document's now-null frame (and would then call into its reset
`ModelContextHost` remote), crashing the renderer:

  iframe.contentDocument.modelContext.registerTool({
    name: 'tool',
    description: 'desc',
    inputSchema: {toJSON() { iframe.remove(); return {}; }},
    execute: () => {},
  });  // Crash.

This CL checks again after serialization, and rejects with the same
`InvalidStateError` as the up-front check. This matches the re-check
added to the spec in
https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp/pull/345.

R=khushalsagar

Allow glicPrivate calls from Google subframes in Google pages

Gemini Web (gemini.google.com/shopping) embeds Universal Cart in a
cross-origin <iframe>. Since crrev.com/c/8028151, the glicPrivate API
rejects any caller that is not the primary main frame, so the embedded
cart cannot show the browser actuation button.

Relax ValidateRenderFrameHost() to also accept subframes whose ancestors
all have HTTPS Google Gemini origins, as long as the frame belongs to
the primary page. It still rejects Google subframes embedded by
non-Gemini pages, which keeps untrusted pages from making Glic act on
their own tab.

glic: Add prefs-backed client data storage API

* Add GlicClientStorage API (getClientStorage) to GlicBrowserHost with synchronous localStorage-like methods and incremental Mojo sync, gated behind features::kGlicClientDataStorage (default enabled).
* Add GlicClientDataStorage on GlicKeyedService to manage authoritative in-memory state and batch writes to prefs::kGlicClientDataStorage.
* Update MaybeMigrateGlicLocalStorage to migrate legacy glicpart localStorage keys into GlicClientDataStorage instead of the default partition.

[BrowserControls] Support hiding controls on toolbar vertical swipe

Allow swiping up on the top toolbar or swiping down on the bottom
toolbar to hide browser controls when BrowserControlsExtraHideGestures
is enabled, browser controls constraints are BOTH, and the controls can
scroll off screen.

While the flag is enabled, vertical toolbar swipes (including the one
that opens the Hub) no longer start or update the toolbar swipe layout,
which only handles horizontal tab swipes, and the Hub swipe direction
follows the live controls position, not the cached toolbar position.

Near the top of the page the hide only sticks together with
https://crrev.com/c/8516678, which stops BrowserControlsOffsetManager
from snapping the controls back to shown when the hide animation
completes. Both changes are behind the flag.

Visual Proof & Screencast Demonstrations:
- Top toolbar, swipe up hides browser controls:
        https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTY3ODA2ODk4NjI4MTk4NHw4YmJmOWQ3Yy1hNw
- Bottom toolbar, swipe down hides browser controls:
        https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTg4MDAzODY4MjUyNTY5Nnw2OTBlYmRlMC1lYg
- Bottom toolbar, swipe up still opens Hub:
        https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NjE0OTY0NDE4MTU2OTUzNnwzZTNjM2ZkZC1mNw

[gpu][media] Retain SharedImage ownership in VideoFrame::WrapSharedImage

This CL removes an obsolete SharedImageInterface::DestroySharedImage
overload (which enforced HasOneRef()) along with its last redundant
callsite in OpenXrGraphicsBindingVulkan.

With that single-ref check removed, the MakeUnowned() call in
VideoFrame::WrapSharedImage() is no longer needed. So this CL also
removes the MakeUnowned() call and guards the behavior behind the
kVideoFrameRetainSharedImageOwnership killswitch. This ensures the
VideoFrame references the original ClientSharedImage instance (instead
of a clone), and as a result, the SyncTokens imported onto the
VideoFrame's SharedImage (e.g. via EndExport) are stored correctly on
the original ClientSharedImage instance.

This CL is a prerequisite before enabling the
UseAutomaticSyncTokenManagement feature.

[browser_actuator] Evict session handlers when factory is unregistered

Observes TransportHandlerFactoryRegistry in TransportSessionImpl via
base::ScopedObservation, implements OnFactoryUnregistered to remove and
destroy any active TransportHandler created by the unregistered factory
and prune it from the session routing table, and resets the observation
in OnRegistryDestroyed.

This prevents session handlers from outliving the KeyedService or test
scope that registered their factory or continuing to receive messages
after unregistration.

Linux: Remove GTK/Qt palette mismatch workarounds

With crrev.com/c/8515993, NativeThemeGtk and NativeThemeQt derive the
color mode from the toolkit palette, so the palette always matches the
color mode for GTK/Qt system themes. The workarounds for a mismatched
palette are no longer needed:

 - Revert the GTK mixer's palette_matches_color_mode check
   (crrev.com/c/8516637). GTK content colors are again set
   unconditionally. The test infrastructure added there is kept since
   NativeThemeGtkTest uses it.
 - Remove the omnibox location icon chip fallback from
   AddNativeChromeColorMixer (part of crrev.com/c/8516937). The toolbar
   color now always contrasts with the omnibox text.

The GTK and Qt contrast guard from crrev.com/c/8516937 is kept, since it
handles themes whose label colors clash with their own window
background, independent of the color mode.

The mismatch unit tests now exercise the matching combinations, which
are the only ones that occur.

Verified under Xvfb + Mutter with a fake portal: GTK Adwaita-dark and
Adwaita, and Qt dark and light palettes, all render chrome://settings
and the omnibox chip readably.

[histogram-cleanup] Remove expired Extensions.Management_Refresh

This removes the Extensions.Management_Refresh histogram, which expired
on 2023-05-07 and was never extended. It timed how long
ExtensionManagement::Refresh() took to reload the enterprise extension
policies, and nobody is looking at that data anymore, so the recording
code is just dead weight. To clean it up I deleted the
SCOPED_UMA_HISTOGRAM_TIMER in ExtensionManagement::Refresh(), dropped
the histogram_macros.h include that only existed for it, and removed
the histogram entry from the extensions histograms.xml.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[Extensions.Management_Refresh]=expired

This change was generated using the skill histogram-cleanup.

[SidePanel] Drop BrowserActions' direct dep on views/side_panel

BrowserActions depended directly on //chrome/browser/ui/views/side_panel
only to ask whether the Comments, History and History Clusters side
panels are supported. Those checks belong with each feature's own code,
not with its Views coordinator.

The Comments and History checks are plain feature flags, so check the
flags directly; the checks go away when those features launch. Move
history_clusters_side_panel_utils, the one check with real logic, to
//chrome/browser/history_clusters next to HistoryClustersServiceFactory,
as glic, contextual tasks and lens already keep their checks in their
own feature code. The function becomes
history_clusters::IsSidePanelSupported(). It keeps the Guest and
Incognito exclusions, hence the side-panel-specific name.

BrowserActions still reaches views/side_panel through the public_deps of
//chrome/browser/ui/lens and //chrome/browser/contextual_tasks:ui. Those
are out of scope here.

No behavior change.

[Masonry] Stretch fragmented grid-lanes items

Grid-lanes items with stacking-axis stretch alignment need their total
stretched size resolved before fragmentation so that each fragment uses
a consistent size.

Retain the original border-box stacking size on alignment candidates and
add the available alignment space once the final candidates are known.

Persist the resulting size on the break token for fragmented layout and
apply it through the existing fixed-size constraints.

This stretch size may expand due to fragmentation break rules in later
changes.

Stretch alignment in the grid axis is already well tested and working as
expected.

🌺 Revert "[Desktop Android] Allow WebAPKs and TWAs to auto-capture top-level links"

This reverts commit df646948374e5c26249f5ee3a71c577a4e4b2803.
Culprit: df646948374e - "[Desktop Android] Allow WebAPKs and TWAs to auto-capture top-level links" (refs/heads/main@{#1718988}, https://crrev.com/c/8535090)

Reason for revert: consistently fails android-internal-desktop-x64-rel.

Mechanism: Since df646948374e landed at #1718988, both
WebApkIntegrationTest#testWebApkTrampoline
("CriteriaNotSatisfiedException: Omnibox chip not found") and the newly
added UrlOverridingTest#testTopLevelNavigationInterceptedForWebApk
("TimeoutException: Navigation didn't fail.") fail deterministically
across android-desktop-17-x64-rel-emu-tests
(https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-desktop-17-x64-rel-emu-tests/4936)
and android-internal-desktop-x64-rel (#31495, #31498). In
ExternalNavigationHandler#shouldBlockExternalNavigationForHttpProtocols,
returning false when pickWebApkIfSoleIntentHandler(...) != null causes
top-level navigations in WebApkIntegrationTest#testWebApkTrampoline to
bypass the in-browser omnibox chip expected by the test, while
testTopLevelNavigationInterceptedForWebApk times out waiting for the
navigation to fail on desktop emulators.

UrlOverridingTest#testTopLevelNavigationInterceptedForWebApk,
WebApkIntegrationTest#testWebApkTrampoline has failed in 3/3 recent
builds of android-internal-desktop-x64-rel, every attempt in every one
of them. This is not flake: it reproduces on every run, so it blocks the
CQ for every unrelated CL that touches this suite. The regression
appears at refs/heads/main@{#1718988}.

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/try/android-internal-desktop-x64-rel/31498

To run/deflake this test on CQ before relanding, add the following
footer to your CL description:
  Include-Ci-Only-Tests: chrome.android.desktop:android-desktop-17-x64-rel-emu-tests,chromium.android.desktop:android-desktop-x64-rel-15-tests|chrome_public_test_apk

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

Original change's description:
> [Desktop Android] Allow WebAPKs and TWAs to auto-capture top-level links
>
> When DesktopAndroidLinkCapturing is enabled on Android Desktop,
> ExternalNavigationDelegateImpl#allowExternalNavigationForHttpProtocols()
> returns false for HTTP/HTTPS URLs so that external navigations stay in
> the browser and surface the "Open in app" omnibox chip instead of
> automatically launching external Android apps. However, installed
> WebAPKs and Trusted Web Activities (TWAs) should still auto-capture
> top-level new-tab (target="_blank") HTTP/HTTPS navigations while
> continuing to keep same-tab and auxiliary popup navigations in the
> browser.
>
> - Update allowExternalNavigationForHttpProtocols() to accept a
>   Supplier<List<ResolveInfo>> (reusing QueryIntentActivitiesSupplier
>   from ExternalNavigationHandler) and return true when
>   TwaValidator.isTwaInstalledForUrl(url, resolveInfoSupplier) is true.
> - Update shouldBlockExternalNavigationForHttpProtocols() in
>   ExternalNavigationHandler to return false when a sole valid WebAPK
>   handler is found via pickWebApkIfSoleIntentHandler().
> - Remove DESKTOP_ANDROID_LINK_CAPTURING from the class-level
>   @DisableFeatures in UrlOverridingTest, replace the obsolete
>   testTopLevelNavigationShouldBeIntercepted test with explicit tests for
>   native apps, TWAs, and WebAPKs on top-level navigations, and disable
>   the mobile CCT native-app handoff tests on Desktop.
>
> Bug: 571579309, 446837985
> Test: TwaValidatorTest, ExternalNavigationHandlerTest#testHttpBlockBypassedByWebApk, UrlOverridingTest#testTopLevelNavigation*

[Keyboard Shortcuts] Add shared IsReservedCommand() in accelerator_table

Extract the reserved browser command list from
BrowserCommandController::IsReservedCommandOrKey() into
IsReservedCommand() in accelerator_table.cc so Desktop and Android can
share a single source of truth for pre-DOM reserved shortcuts without
duplicating the command list.

On Desktop, BrowserCommandController::IsReservedCommandOrKey() now
delegates its final command check to IsReservedCommand() with no
behavior change. On Android, IsReservedCommand() also reserves pane
navigation (IDC_FOCUS_NEXT_PANE and IDC_FOCUS_PREVIOUS_PANE for F6 /
Shift+F6) so web pages cannot trap keyboard focus.

[icu] Add ICU NumberFormat and UResourceBundle tests

Add unit tests covering ICU NumberFormat numbering systems, currency
formatting and symbols (including when a non-currency DecimalFormat is
later reconfigured to format currency or queried for currency symbols),
and concurrent UResourceBundle / NumberFormat operations across
locales. They will be used to validate that an upcoming set of ICU
optimizations preserve existing behavior.

Also add FormatPercent_Concurrent perftest to capture the impact of
these optimization CLs.

Upcoming optimization CLs:
- CL 1 (https://crrev.com/c/8564041): Reuse NumberingSystem in
  DecimalFormatSymbols and NumberFormatterImpl
- CL 2 (https://crrev.com/c/8573417): Skip currency resource loading for
  non-currency NumberFormat styles
- CL 3 (https://crrev.com/c/8568883): Scope gResbMutex to parent-pointer
  link and replace refcount lock with atomic

[WebAudio] Clamp hardware buffer limits in GetOutputBufferSize

When the OS audio manager reports a minimum or maximum hardware buffer
size outside WebAudio's [kMinWebAudioBufferSize, kMaxWebAudioBufferSize]
range, RendererWebAudioDeviceImpl::GetOutputBufferSize() only clamped
min_buffer_size from below and max_buffer_size from above. If the
reported min_hardware_buffer_size exceeded kMaxWebAudioBufferSize
(8192), min_buffer_size became larger than max_buffer_size (e.g., 16384
> 8192), causing AudioLatency::GetExactBufferSize() to hit a fatal
DCHECK_LE or return an invalid buffer size.

Changes:
- Use std::clamp() in RendererWebAudioDeviceImpl::GetOutputBufferSize()
  to bound both min_buffer_size and max_buffer_size to
  [kMinWebAudioBufferSize, kMaxWebAudioBufferSize].
- Re-enable
  ExactLatency_HighHardwareBufferSize_CapsAtMaxBufferSize in
  renderer_webaudiodevice_impl_unittest.cc.

[3/N] WebMCP: Introduce the `Tool` interface object

This CL replaces the `RegisteredTool` dictionary returned by
`getTools()` and accepted by `executeTool()` with a `Tool` interface
object. Each `Tool` carries the non-web-exposed `tool_id` of the tool it
represents. `executeTool()`, including cross-document execution through
the browser, now targets tools by that ID rather than by name.

This fixes the execution-time race described in the parent CL. If a
page unregisters a tool and registers a new one under the same name,
executing the stale `Tool` used to run the new tool. Now it rejects.
The new WPT
external/wpt/webmcp/imperative/tool-re-registration-race.https.html
exercises this.

When the ID isn't found, the rejection message is deliberately generic
so the ID is not leaked to web content. DevTools still receives the ID
via the probe.

Embedders (the actor) and DevTools still identify tools by name, via
`ModelContext::ExecuteToolByName()`, so they remain subject to the race.
Moving them to IDs is follow-up work.

See
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1psoB7k71-Dgkxg2tTG62DYJDTg02x8zOS3jCEd0QlbM/edit?tab=t.0.

R=mfoltz

[Omnibox] Defer AI Mode popup creation

Design doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P7h7q6zqhxgPtKhVJBUAU9eb1pawDwK66iQu8CTeRSs/edit?resourcekey=0-nPCcl7S22YgfphQ-H6WV5Q&tab=t.0

When a browser window is built, OmniboxPopupAimPresenter creates the AI
Mode popup's WebUI content in its constructor: a WebContents and its
navigation to the AI Mode popup page. The navigation's IPCs and the
page load then compete with the new window's first frame on the browser
UI thread and in the shared top-chrome renderer. The AI Mode popup is
opened far less often than the regular results popup, so it does not
need to be ready that early.

This CL adds a disabled-by-default feature,
OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation. With it, the presenter does not create
the content in its constructor. It overrides the new
OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::CreateWebUIContent(), and
OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::EnsureWebUIContentCreated() calls it on
whichever of these comes first:

- A task posted after the browser window presents its first frame.
- OmniboxPopupPresenterBase::Show().
- The regular popup's context menu, which acts on the AI Mode
  WebContents.

The presenter asks for that frame itself: its constructor makes a
one-off RequestSuccessfulPresentationTimeForNextFrame() call on the
compositor of the location bar's widget. Both LocationBarView and
WebUILocationBar build the presenter while the window is built, before
its first paint, so the next frame is the window's first frame. The
presenter posts the creation task at most once.

The presentation task is what keeps the work out of the window's first
frame. A fixed delay from window creation could not do that: on Linux
and macOS the window is activated inside its own show call, before the
first paint, and the time to first paint varies by device. There is
also no fallback timer. A requested callback is kept until a frame
presents successfully. A window that is never presented never shows
the popup either, and the on-show path covers any open. A presenter
that is created after the first paint, because the profile became
eligible for AI Mode later, gets the next presented frame or its first
show.

With the feature disabled, creation is unchanged.

  out/Default/browser_tests \
  --gtest_filter='OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation*:*WithoutDeferCreation' && \
  out/Default/unit_tests \
  --gtest_filter='OmniboxPopupPresenterBaseTest.*'

[Omnibox] Show side panel icon before AskG side panel description

Follow-up to the Omnibox_AskGSuggestionSidePanelDescription param. Per
the mock, "Opens in side panel" is preceded by a side panel
(dock_to_right) icon in the WebUI omnibox popup.

Add ContextualSearchProvider::HasSidePanelDescription(), which tells
whether a given match shows the side panel description: the AskG
entrypoint match, or a contextual suggestion with a description.

Add an optional `description_icon_path` to the searchbox mojom match.
WebuiOmniboxHandler sets it to the new dock_to_right.svg for matches
where HasSidePanelDescription() is true.

cr-searchbox-match renders the icon as a ::before of #secondaryText (the
description), so it picks up the existing show/hide rules for contextual
suggestion descriptions without new CSS for them. The icon is mirrored
in RTL, where the cobrowse side panel opens on the other side.

Only the WebUI omnibox popup sets the field, and only when the param is
enabled. Other searchboxes default it to empty.

db6a52c455fd3c8c78b35555c8fb81e4f12634b7 [ diff ] 
Linux: Take Chrome UI color mode from the GTK/Qt theme

When a GTK or Qt system theme is in use, Chrome UI is painted with the
toolkit's colors, but its light/dark color mode came from the
process-wide OsSettingsProvider, i.e. the xdg-desktop-portal
color-scheme preference. Since crrev.com/c/8429688, portal "no
preference" resolves to light, so a dark-only toolkit theme (e.g.
Adwaita-dark, or a dark Qt palette) produced light-mode Material
surfaces painted with the theme's light text, e.g. #EEEEEC on white in
chrome://settings.

Instead, give NativeTheme a virtual CalculatePreferredColorScheme() and
have NativeThemeGtk and NativeThemeQt derive the scheme from the
toolkit's window background color, so the color mode always matches the
colors the toolkit mixers supply. The process-wide override (e.g.
--force-dark-mode) still takes precedence.

The portal preference is unchanged for everything else: the Classic
theme, the web NativeTheme instance and incognito web contents still
follow it, so crbug.com/462191707 stays fixed. The preference also still
reaches GTK via gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme, so themes that ship
both variants (e.g. Adwaita) switch, and Chrome UI follows.

Also:
 - OsSettingsProviderGtk no longer listens for gtk-theme-name and
   gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme itself. Its handler ran before
   GtkUi cleared the style color cache, so observers recomputed from
   stale colors. GtkUi::OnThemeChanged() now notifies the provider after
   clearing the cache.
 - GtkUi::LoadGtkValues() and ThemeService::BrowserUsesDarkColors() use
   the toolkit-derived scheme when a system theme is in use.

Verified under Xvfb + Mutter with a fake portal:
  GTK Adwaita-dark, portal light: dark, readable (was low contrast)
  GTK Adwaita, portal dark: Adwaita switches to dark, Chrome dark
  GTK Adwaita, portal light: light
  Qt dark palette, portal light: dark, readable
  Classic, Adwaita-dark, portal light: light

New NativeThemeGtkTest unit tests fail without this change.

[a11y] Rename WebContentsAccessibilityAndroid to WebContentsAccessibilityBase

Android accessibility will be able to run on a background thread. Then
this class becomes the shared base of two subclasses: one for the
UI-thread mode of today, and one for background mode. This CL only
renames the class, so that the split in the next CL is easy to read.

It also renames the native parameters in Java, because the JNI
generator uses their names to find the C++ class. Comments, docs and
histogram text that name the class change too.

The browser test uses the base for one CL. The next CL moves it to the
new subclass.

No behavior change.

Based on a prototype by dtseng@ (crrev.com/c/8258117).

[Linux] Prevent QT from loading GTK3 when GSettings schemas are invalid

On Wayland, GDK3 reads font rendering settings with
g_settings_get_enum(), which calls g_error() and aborts if a key is
missing or is not an enum. GtkUi already refuses to initialize on such
systems (crbug.com/434763642), but Chrome then falls back to QtUi. On
GTK-based desktops, QT loads its GTK3 platform theme plugin
(libqgtk3.so), which calls gtk_init() and crashes in exactly the way
GtkUi tried to avoid.

This CL:
- Moves the schema validation from ui/gtk to ui/base/glib as
  ui::AreGdkWaylandFontSchemasValid() so it can be shared with ui/qt.
- Extends QT's existing GTK3 prevention (previously only applied when
  GTK4 is loaded) to also apply on Wayland when the schemas are invalid.
- Records the reason for invalid schemas in a crash key
  (gdk-wayland-font-schema-error) to help diagnose misconfigured
  systems.

Tested with a deliberately broken org.gnome.desktop.interface schema
(missing font-hinting) under a headless Wayland compositor: GTK3 aborts
with "does not contain a key named 'font-hinting'", while Chrome with
this CL falls back to QT without loading libqgtk3.so or libgtk-3.

[ipcz] Remove same-process transport exception for mojo::DirectReceiver

`mojo::DirectReceiver` creates a pair of dedicated transport endpoints
using `CreateTransportPair()`: `transports.first` (the global endpoint)
is passed to the broker node while `transports.second` (the local
endpoint) is used by the `ThreadLocalNode` that backs `DirectReceiver`.
If the creating process is a broker process, the global endpoint is
connected to the in-process local broker node; otherwise, it is
forwarded to the remote broker node via `IPCZ_CONNECT_NODE_SHARE_BROKER`.

When constructing a `mojo::DirectReceiver` in a non-broker process,
`CreateTransportPair()` configures the global endpoint as a non-broker
endpoint (`EndpointType::kNonBroker`) even though the global endpoint
is adopted by a broker. The remote broker node ignores the `kNonBroker`
designation and adopts its endpoint with the correct configuration (a
`kBroker` source and a `kNonBroker` destination); however, the local
endpoint is left configured as a link between two non-broker endpoints.

On Windows, a non-broker endpoint only transmits handles or accepts
pre-duplicated (`kRecipient`) handles when its peer is a `kBroker` (or
explicitly trusted). To make handle transfer work despite the
misconfigured endpoint type, https://crrev.com/c/4429594 set the local
endpoint's remote process to `base::Process::Current()` and added
`remote_process.is_current()` exceptions to `CanTransmitHandles()` and
`DecodeHandle()`.

Remove the need for these workarounds by creating the transport
endpoints with the right initial configuration.

[NTP] Extract chrome://new-tab-page loadTimeData into a helper

Moves the loadTimeData of chrome://new-tab-page out of
CreateAndAddNewTabPageUiHtmlSource() into
NewTabPageUI::GetLoadTimeData(), which returns it as a base::DictValue.
CreateAndAddNewTabPageUiHtmlSource() adds the returned values to the
WebUIDataSource.

This lets surfaces that reuse NTP elements outside of the WebUI, such
as the NTP Lite component extension, use the same loadTimeData instead
of duplicating it. No behavior change for chrome://new-tab-page.

[WebView] Add unit test for destroying AwPacProcessor with pending jobs

AwPacProcessor tracks in-flight SetProxyScriptJob and
MakeProxyRequestJob instances in its `jobs_` set on the AwPacProcessor
task runner so they can be cancelled to unblock waiting caller threads
when the processor is destroyed while requests are still in progress.

https://crrev.com/c/8410291 updated AwPacProcessor job cancellation to
drain `jobs_` using a `while (!jobs_.empty())` loop in
CancelJobsOnPacThread() so that erasing each cancelled job from `jobs_`
does not invalidate an active std::set iterator.

Add a C++ unit test (`AwPacProcessorTest.DestroyWithPendingJobs`)
verifying that destroying an AwPacProcessor while multiple proxy
resolution requests are in flight cleanly cancels all pending jobs and
unblocks the calling threads.

  --gtest_filter="AwPacProcessorTest.*"

The vertical scrollbar on the app menu list view was previously disabled
to avoid conflicting with a button inside the menu. Since that button
has been removed, the scrollbar can now be re-enabled.

restoring the default ListView scrollbar behavior, and cleans up the
associated plumbing across AppMenu, AppMenuHandlerImpl, and
AppMenuDelegate.

Extensions: IconVariants: Support manifest schema and core icon sets

Add manifest parsing, schema validation, and icon set resolution for
the icon_variants key.

- Validate uniform file extensions per icon group in
  ExtensionIconVariant.
- Store the "any" icon in a dedicated slot in ExtensionIconSet, used
  by Get() as a fallback when no sized icon matches. It isn't stored
  as EXTENSION_ICON_GIGANTOR, since 512 is a real icon size.
- Merge multiple variant dictionaries in IconVariantsInfo into light
  and dark icon sets. Icons from a variant with explicit color_schemes
  override those from a variant without; otherwise the first variant
  to provide a size (or "any") wins.
- Register icon variant paths in ExtensionsClient.

6022f5664ff747b747764a66a22a28ac4497b70b [ diff ] 
[IME] Speed up GetCompositionCharacterBounds()

In WebInputMethodControllerImpl, GetCompositionCharacterBounds() called
WebLocalFrameImpl::FirstRectForCharacterRange() for every character of
the composition. Each call converts a plain text offset to a range by
walking the editable from its start. With a large textarea or
contenteditable and the caret near the end, typing with an IME became
very slow as the composition grew.

The new algorithm walks the editable once with a single
CharacterIterator, advancing it to the start of the composition and then
one character at a time. The iterator uses the scope and behavior that
CompositionRange() uses to compute the composition's plain text offsets,
so the characters it visits line up with those offsets. It relies on
CompositionRange() having already updated style and layout, rather than
updating them again for each character.

The new code is guarded by the FastCompositionCharacterBounds runtime
feature (enabled by default). The tests check that it produces the same
bounds as the legacy code including for compositions that start at the
end of a block.

[downloads] Create a download state model for multiple call sites

Create a download state model to help offer a single source of truth
for download state given there will be multiple reference call sites
like the download toolbar button progress ring and dropdown tray. The
previous implementation was only in the controller.

Attempt to deflake CustomTabActivityTests in cluster

This CL increases waitForDeferredStartup timeout to 20s.
ChromeActivityTestRule#waitForDeferredStartup() already waits up to 20s
for deferred startup to be posted, but only waited 3s for deferred
startup to finish. On android-desktop builders, finishing all deferred
startup tasks frequently takes longer than 3s, causing tests that launch
activities via startActivityCompletely() to flake.

[RTS] Enable RTS test skipping for android_sync_integration_tests on android-16-x64-rel

This enables RTS (Regression Test Selection) filtering for
android_sync_integration_tests on android-16-x64-rel (mirrored by
android-x64-rel and android-16-x64-rel try builders).

Potential savings:
~332.6 bot-hours daily / ~13.86 bot-hours/hour (4 shards, 57.8% of test time skipped).
